tagline: Waterfall country at the foot of Khao Yai near Bangkok, with rafting, camping, and local fruit
introHtml:
Nakhon Nayok sits just northeast of Bangkok, only a couple of hours out via the Rangsit–Ongkharak road. The first thing most people picture is the waterfalls at the foot of Khao Yai — both Nang Rong and Sarika falls, where Bangkokians regularly come to splash around and beat the heat. It's a small province with the Khao Yai range rising up behind it.

Beyond the waterfalls there's Khun Dan Prakan Chon, a long roller-compacted concrete dam with wide reservoir viewpoints. The Ban Lao Rian side is the base for rafting and riverside adventure activities on the Nakhon Nayok River. Food runs from punchy Nakhon Nayok som tam to mayongchid and sweet marian plums and egg bananas, plus riverside restaurants and mountain-view cafes lined up along the road to the falls.
bestTime: June–October the falls run full and are fun to play in, while November–February brings cool, comfortable weather good for camping, cycling, and exploring the foothills. March–April is the season when mayongchid and marian plums come into fruit

highlights.name: Nang Rong Waterfall
highlights.blurb: A waterfall at the foot of Khao Yai that draws plenty of Bangkokians to swim, with pools to soak in and riverside eateries — the first thing that comes to mind with Nakhon Nayok.

highlights.name: Sarika Waterfall
highlights.blurb: A tall waterfall that drops down the cliff in tiers, strong and pretty in the rainy season. You can hike up to see each level and eat by the water.

highlights.name: Khun Dan Prakan Chon Dam
highlights.blurb: A long roller-compacted concrete dam at the foot of the hills, with wide reservoir viewpoints. You can drive up to take photos and catch the cool breeze.

highlights.name: Nakhon Nayok River rafting
highlights.blurb: In the rainy season the Nakhon Nayok River runs strong, with rafting on rubber boats and tubes on offer — the most popular adventure activity around here.

highlights.name: Wang Takhrai
highlights.blurb: A wide forest park along the stream with big shady trees, where you can wade in the shallows and camp by the water.

highlights.name: Khao Yai foothills, Nakhon Nayok side
highlights.blurb: The road up to the falls is lined with resorts, mountain-view cafes, and camping spots — a place to escape Bangkok and sleep in the cool air.

foodScene.name: Nakhon Nayok som tam
foodScene.note: The som tam here is known for being bold and made many different ways. Several well-known shops along the road to the falls are worth a stop, paired with grilled chicken.

foodScene.name: Mayongchid and sweet marian plums
foodScene.note: The province's signature local fruit, in season around March–April, with sweet-tart flesh. Buy them fresh from the orchards to take home as a gift.

foodScene.name: Waterfall-side food
foodScene.note: Restaurants by the streams around Nang Rong and Sarika serve grilled fish, prawns, tom yum, and made-to-order dishes — eaten with your feet dipped in the cool water.

foodScene.name: Egg bananas and local snacks
foodScene.note: Nakhon Nayok egg bananas are small, sweet, and fragrant, eaten fresh or made into banana chips and sun-dried banana, sold as gifts at markets and roadside stalls.

foodScene.name: Isan food
foodScene.note: Som tam, larb, and grilled chicken are easy to find around town and at the waterfall spots — bold and tasty, an easy meal with plenty of shops.

foodScene.name: Mountain-view cafes
foodScene.note: The roads up to the dam and the falls have several new cafes with mountain and rice-field views — a spot to sip coffee in the cool breeze between sights.

foodScene.name: Noodles and street food in town
foodScene.note: The market district in central Nakhon Nayok has noodle shops and walk-and-eat snacks at local prices, with plenty to choose from.

foodScene.name: Mu kratha
foodScene.note: A popular dinner for locals and groups out camping at the falls, with several shops to choose from at friendly prices.

attractions.name: Nang Rong Waterfall
attractions.blurb: A popular waterfall at the foot of Khao Yai with pools to swim in and riverside eateries — Bangkokians come here in numbers to beat the heat.

attractions.name: Sarika Waterfall
attractions.blurb: A tall waterfall dropping in tiers from the cliff. You can hike up to see each level and eat by the stream.

attractions.name: Khun Dan Prakan Chon Dam
attractions.blurb: A long roller-compacted concrete dam at the foot of the hills, with wide reservoir viewpoints. You can drive up to take photos and catch the cool breeze.

attractions.name: Wang Takhrai
attractions.blurb: A shady forest park along the stream with big trees, shallow water to wade in, and camping by the water — great for a family trip.

attractions.name: Ganesha Park (largest statue)
attractions.blurb: A plaza enshrining a giant reclining Ganesha statue, a popular spot for paying respects, making wishes, and taking photos in the province.

attractions.name: Wat Khao Nang Buat
attractions.blurb: A temple on a hill overlooking the town and the wide fields. You can climb up to pay respects and take in the foothill views.

attractions.name: Nakhon Nayok River rafting
attractions.blurb: A rainy-season adventure, riding rubber boats and tubes down the rapids, with full services at points along the river.

attractions.name: Markets and the Nakhon Nayok town center
attractions.blurb: The town center has markets and local food shops to graze, worth a stop before or after heading up to the waterfall side.
